detailed_description: Text Extractor pulls common token types out of pasted text using a small set of fixed regular expressions. Pick a type from email, URL, phone, IP, number, hashtag, mention, or All, click Extract, and the tool runs the matching pattern (or all patterns) over the input and shows deduplicated results. Each result has a Copy button, single-type results have a Copy All button, and All mode groups results by type with per-type counts. Load Example fills in a sample multi-language string, Clear empties the input. The tool does not do RFC 5322 / E.164 validation, Unicode normalization, custom delimiters, capture-group editing, file upload, or CSV/JSON export.
usage_steps: Paste or type raw text into the input textarea, or click Load Example for sample data
Pick a type from the dropdown: email, URL, phone, IP, number, hashtag, mention, or All
Click Extract to run the matching regex and deduplicate results
Hover any result to see its Copy button and copy a single value
In single-type mode, use Copy All to copy every result joined by newlines
Click Clear to reset the input and results
usage_examples: Pull every email out of a long support ticket dump for follow-up
Grab every URL from a markdown article to feed into a link checker
Run All mode on a chat log to see hashtags, mentions, and phone numbers grouped together
Extract IP addresses from a server log snippet before pasting them into another tool
